mechanism: Hidden-truth faults are scattered around (not on) mapped Quaternary traces; a scatter-smoothed (gaussian sigma=1.85 px) off-catalogue far-field emission (catalogue distance >= 3 px = 300 m), dot-thinned at d=1.5 px, targets the habitat that carries 81.4% of the live 0.2477 emission's dots. The emission-time detector is a HistGradientBoosting fitted on ALL published labels (same instrument as Slot 5 / Addendum E). Dot-thinning at d=1.5 keeps credit per dot near saturation (~3) while minimising false-positive mass (cost stays 1 per dot), a pure emission-geometry effect validated live on H19-5->d1.5 (0.1922->0.2477).
named_non_fault_mimic_process: Alluvial fan edges, playa shorelines, and volcanic cone rims can produce linear topographic and radiometric responses that mimic fault scarps; lidar lappos_max (best single-channel AUC 0.58) does not discriminate these from true faults. The far-field restriction (d_cat >= 3 px) specifically avoids catalogue traces, so the mimic risk is geomorphic lineaments rather than known faults.
holdout_note: NOT MEASURABLE on the catalogue-internal component-hidden holdout by design: 100% of proxy truth lies at d=0 from the published catalogue and 99.6% of credit is earned within 200 m, while this emission is entirely at d_cat >= 3 px (far field). Holdout DTI = 0 by construction; this is the documented 'holdout cannot see the far field' limit (knowledge/10). Support comes from GEMSDOE32's generative truth model (+0.0247, 12/12 draws positive for scatter-smoothed off-catalogue emission) and convergence of GEMSDOE32 (0.2778) and GEMSDOE36 PINN (0.2750) on the same B2 + ~38k optimum.
